1. `import tempfile` — the ONE new stdlib import this feature adds (L79–86 block).
2. `_now_iso()` — Z-suffixed UTC ISO-8601 formatter. It does NOT exist today (grep confirms 0 hits); R4 introduces it.
3. `STATE_VERB_STAGES: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = ("forge-0-epic", *PRODUCTION_STAGES)` — the verbs' `--stage` domain. **CRITICAL: `PRODUCTION_STAGES` already exists at L99** as a 6-entry, ORDER-SENSITIVE tuple consumed by `next_stage()` (L245), `verify_state` (L317) and `stage_exit` (L1602–1604). items.title: Add the state-complete verb with version bump and staleness cascade
items.description:
Add the `state-complete` verb to `scripts/forge-session.py` (tests in `tests/test_state_verbs.py`) — the most complex R4 verb: completion, version bump, `basedOnVersions`, artifacts, the two-commit hash follow-up, and the deterministic downstream staleness cascade that replaces a hand-computed step.

`state-complete --feature --stage --version --based-on STAGE=N (repeatable) --artifact PATH (repeatable) [--commit-hash H] [--status complete|in-progress] [--resumable] [--preserve-commit-hash] --specs-dir [--epic] [--json]`

Three branches:
1. `--commit-hash` given → set ONLY `commitHash`, leaving status/version/artifacts intact (Commit 2 of the Git Commit Protocol). GUARD: if the stage's current `status` is not `"complete"`, raise `UsageError(f"--commit-hash requires {stage} to be complete (status: {actual!r}); run state-complete without --commit-hash first")` — otherwise a typo'd `--stage` writes a lone `{"commitHash": …}` entry that violates `stageEntry`'s `required: ["status"]` at exit 0.
2. `--resumable` given (and no `--commit-hash`) → record ONLY `status: "in-progress"` plus the `updatedAt` refresh; no cascade. `--resumable` together with an explicit `--status complete` is a contradiction: raise `UsageError("--resumable implies --status in-progress; do not pass --status complete")` (owner decision 2026-07-29 — reject rather than silently override).
3. Otherwise (including a bare `--status in-progress`, forge-5-loop's partial completion) → set `status` (from `--status`, default `"complete"`), `completedAt`, `version`, `basedOnVersions`, `artifacts`, and `commitHash = None` UNLESS `--preserve-commit-hash` is passed. Then apply the staleness cascade.

**Two distinct in-progress uses — do NOT conflate them (owner decision 2026-07-29).** `--status in-progress` has two sanctioned callers, and they need OPPOSITE behavior:
  - **Partial completion** (forge-5-loop Step 5, spec 03 §11.2 row 14): the stage really did produce artifacts, it just is not finished. Write `completedAt`, `version`, `basedOnVersions` and `artifacts` exactly as the complete branch does — only `status` differs. This is why item 013 passes `--based-on forge-4-backlog=N` on that call; those flags must NOT be silently discarded.
  - **Failed-Commit-1 revert** (shared-conventions L245): the stage did NOT complete. Signalled by the new **`--resumable`** flag (which implies `--status in-progress`). Record ONLY `status` plus the usual `updatedAt` refresh: do NOT write `completedAt`, `version`, `basedOnVersions` or `artifacts`, do NOT reset `commitHash`, and SKIP the staleness cascade. The frozen contract is 'leave state as in-progress so the stage can be resumed'; stamping a completion timestamp, bumping the version, or cascading staleness off a commit that never landed are all behavioral changes in a zero-behavioral-diff feature.
Schema validation CANNOT distinguish these (stageEntry declares `status` and `completedAt` as independent optional properties), so both branches need dedicated tests.

Cascade: for each downstream stage whose recorded `basedOnVersions` references an older version of the completed stage, set its status to `"stale"`. Key this off a `_CASCADE_TARGETS` map, not off `PRODUCTION_STAGES` ordering.

`--based-on` parsing: `STAGE=N`; a token without `=` or with a non-integer N raises `UsageError`.

The `--status` and `--preserve-commit-hash` flags exist for the two frozen recovery branches of the Git Commit Protocol — see notes.
acceptanceCriteria: With the default --status complete, state-complete sets status, completedAt, version, basedOnVersions, artifacts and commitHash: null, and the result validates against pipeline-state-schema.json
--commit-hash on a complete stage sets only commitHash, leaving status, version and artifacts intact
--commit-hash against a stage that is not complete exits 2 with the specified UsageError message

--status in-progress WITHOUT --resumable (forge-5-loop's partial completion) records status 'in-progress' but still writes completedAt, version, basedOnVersions and artifacts exactly as the complete branch does - a --based-on value passed on that call is never silently discarded, and like the complete branch it resets commitHash to null unless --preserve-commit-hash is passed AND fires the downstream staleness cascade. Only status differs between --status complete and a bare --status in-progress

--resumable (the failed-Commit-1 revert, shared-conventions L245) records ONLY status 'in-progress' plus the updatedAt refresh: completedAt absent/null, version unchanged, basedOnVersions and artifacts unchanged, commitHash unchanged, and NO staleness cascade - asserted by a dedicated test, not by schema validation alone (the schema permits completedAt on an in-progress entry, so validation cannot catch a regression here)

items.description:
REQ-PORT-03 / SC-5. This is the FINAL cross-unit reconciliation and fixture-refresh sweep — items 001/002/004/005/006/007/008/009/010/011/012/013/015 each already regenerated adapters/ in their own commit, so this item verifies the combined end state rather than performing the first regeneration. Every moved or split reference file must reach all six adapter targets: `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `pi` (`scripts/build-adapters.py` `AGENT_TARGETS`, L49 — six, not the five the specs originally said; the Pi target landed in 0.13.0).

1. Run the adapter build and regenerate `adapters/` for all six targets: `.venv-adapters/bin/python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` (create the venv first if absent: `python3 -m venv .venv-adapters && .venv-adapters/bin/python3 -m pip install -q -r scripts/requirements-adapters.txt`). The generator needs a YAML dependency, so prefer the gitignored `.venv-adapters/bin/python3` interpreter — the same preference `tests/test_build_adapters.py::_generator_interpreter()` encodes. A bare `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` may fail with an import error that is easy to misdiagnose as a build failure.
2. Refresh the gemini fixture using the minimal-canon SCRATCH-BUILD plus `command cp -f` procedure — build `--root minimal-canon` into a scratch dir, then copy that output into the fixture. Do NOT copy the real adapter; that re-introduces host-translated tokens.
3. Confirm every new/moved reference file appears under `adapters/pi/` as well as under the five agent bundles. Pi resolves references through its own extension (`adapter-src/pi/`), so a path verified on five hosts can still be broken on the sixth — that is the #122/#132 failure class.
4. Update `tests/test_build_adapters.py`'s own local `AGENT_TARGETS` constant (L38) from the five-tuple to the six-tuple `("claude", "codex", "copilot", "cursor", "gemini", "pi")`, matching `scripts/build-adapters.py` L49. This is UNCONDITIONAL — a five-tuple test constant can never assert the `adapters/pi/` presence AC below. Run the file's tests and fix any per-target assertion that assumed five targets.
5. Confirm no moved content carries a Claude-only token in any file a non-Claude host reads (REQ-PORT-02) by RUNNING the existing gate: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_adapter_host_neutrality.py`, which applies the canonical `FORBIDDEN_TOKENS` tuple (```Agent` tool``, ```Skill` tool``, ```Monitor` tool``, `/clear`, `AskUserQuestion`, …) to every non-Claude bundle. Do not eyeball this. NOTE its deliberate scope limits: it scans non-Claude SKILL BODIES only and skips any path with `references` in its parts, because bundled reference docs are copied verbatim and may legitimately quote a tool name (see its module docstring); and `NON_CLAUDE_TARGETS` excludes `adapters/pi/`, because the pi host implements AskUserQuestion. **Do NOT widen either scope here** — ~25 committed reference files per non-Claude target already carry FORBIDDEN_TOKENS by design, so widening goes red on pre-existing content, and the only way to green it would be rewording frozen text (violating REQ-BEHAV-01 and item 001's byte-for-byte rule). Instead confirm the move introduced no NEW token: for each moved/created reference file, its FORBIDDEN_TOKENS census equals that of its source span. Expect a non-zero but UNCHANGED census for findings-template.md (AskUserQuestion, from source verification-checklists.md L395) and agent-selection.md (AskUserQuestion, from runner-contract.md L95) — verbatim-move survivors.
